name: power_tuning
description: Section 8 (compat, no numbered test): every read restores the code defaults, then loads the exemplar's properties ('default' curve pattern). Without an exemplar: R 2, funding-efficiency curve (0,0)(100,100)(120,110) -> 90 at x = 90, pole curve (0,-0.02)(120,0.01) -> -0.005 at 60, funding-decay (0,1)(1,1) -> 1, usage-decay -> 1, strike response (0,20)(100,100) -> 60 at 50, max funding 1.2 (code default, float32 literal 0x3F99999A), strike efficiency 0.5, strike duration 10, min acceptable funding 0.6 (0x3F19999A). Shipped: efficiency curve 80 at 90, pole curve 0 at 50, 0.025 at 100 and -0.0125 at 12.5, usage-decay 0.45 at 0.5, funding-decay 1.1 at 0, strike response 75 at 50, duration 12; the 'f32 x 0.01' values multiply by the float constant 0.01f with one 24-bit rounding (8, PW8; checked in Python/numpy): max funding 120 -> 1.1999999 (0x3F999999, not 1.2), strike efficiency 20 -> 0.19999999 (0x3E4CCCCC), min acceptable funding 60 -> 0.59999996 (0x3F199999), max production ratio 110 -> 1.1 (0x3F8CCCCD), min funding to end a strike 90 -> 0.9 (0x3F666666). TuningReload re-reads it and refreshes the ordinance factor (0x0911E117). A removed curve property falls back to its code default; [choice] a scalar curve property counts as absent, an empty array gives an empty curve (0.0). Percent values are x 0.01f: 150 -> 1.5. R 3 widens the wiring.
